en.html:
They say that when a smith turns himself into an armor, he changes not only his body but his soul into steel.

So, although a true-forged armor holds a <ruby>mind<rt>mind</rt></ruby>, it is supposed to be very flat, with hardly a ripple of feeling in it... normally.

Masamune was nothing like that. He was as emotional as a human being, or more so.

But right now he was giving out exactly the voice an armor ought to have: cold, hard iron.

They say that when a smith turns himself into an armor, he changes not only his body but his soul into steel.

So, although a true-forged armor holds a mindmind, it is supposed to be very flat, with hardly a ripple of feeling in it... normally.

Masamune was nothing like that. He was as emotional as a human being, or more so.

But right now he was giving out exactly the voice an armor ought to have: cold, hard iron.

en.text:
The wing armorwings was gone, nearly half of it blown away.

Very bad.

In this state we could not keep flying. Pour heat into regeneration...◆ no, there was no chance it would finish in time.

What was left of the wing armor just barely held our balancebalance. We probably would not die from the fall.

But that only meant the enemy, perfectly healthy, would be free to beat us to death at his leisure.

A warrior who can fly against one who cannot: the fighting strength is one to three, oror one to five. Some even say one to ten.

In short, no contest.
